Skill 1.1.1: Extract Data from S3, EBS, EFS, RDS, DynamoDB & OpenSearch
tasks.topic: Domain 1: Data Preparation for ML & AI
tasks.subtopic: Task 1.1: Collect and store data
tasks.description: Think of data extraction as picking the right pipeline for your data warehouse. Amazon S3 is your central unlimited lake. Amazon EBS is a high-speed hard drive attached to a single EC2 instance for fast local scratch files. Amazon EFS is a shared network folder that multiple notebook instances or training nodes can mount at the same time. RDS and DynamoDB hold operational transactional data, while OpenSearch provides fast text search.
tasks.notes: Exam Tip: For multi-node shared storage choose EFS/FSx; for general datasets choose S3 Fast File mode. Gotcha: Choosing Amazon EBS for distributed multi-node training. EBS CANNOT be shared across multiple instances! Choose EFS or FSx Lustre instead.

tasks.title: Skill 1.1.2: Storage Decisions Based on Cost, Performance & Compliance
tasks.topic: Domain 1: Data Preparation for ML & AI
tasks.subtopic: Task 1.1: Collect and store data
tasks.description: Storage isn't one-size-fits-all. S3 Standard is for active training data. S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically moves data to colder tiers when access drops without performance penalty. S3 Glacier is for compliance archives. For highest compute throughput during deep learning, FSx for Lustre caches directly from S3.
tasks.notes: Exam Tip: Use Intelligent-Tiering when access patterns are unpredictable to avoid manual lifecycle policies. Gotcha: Picking Glacier for models that retrain weekly. Glacier retrieval latency takes hours and incurs retrieval costs!

tasks.title: Skill 1.1.4: Real-Time Streaming Ingestion (Kinesis, Flink, Kafka)
tasks.topic: Domain 1: Data Preparation for ML & AI
tasks.subtopic: Task 1.1: Collect and store data
tasks.description: When data arrives in continuous live streams (like user clicks, sensor feeds, or live chat), Amazon Kinesis Data Streams captures millions of events per second with sub-second latency. Kinesis Data Firehose buffers and converts formats before writing to S3. Apache Flink runs stateful real-time window calculations.
tasks.notes: Exam Tip: If you need immediate streaming feature calculation (<200ms), use Kinesis Streams + Lambda/Flink; if loading to S3/OpenSearch, use Firehose. Gotcha: Confusing Kinesis Streams and Firehose. Firehose CANNOT do custom consumer sub-second push; it buffers data for at least 60 seconds.

tasks.description: Vector databases store numerical representations (embeddings) of text, code, or images so you can find 'conceptually similar' items. tasks.title: Skill 1.1.9: SageMaker Feature Store (Online vs Offline Store)
tasks.topic: Domain 1: Data Preparation for ML & AI
tasks.subtopic: Task 1.1: Collect and store data
tasks.description: Feature Store is the single source of truth for computed ML features. The Online Store (built on low-latency storage) serves features in under 10ms for live model inference. The Offline Store (in Amazon S3) maintains historical point-in-time features for batch training and prevents data leakage.
tasks.notes: Exam Tip: Use the Online Store for sub-10ms inference and the Offline Store for reproducible training sets. Gotcha: Querying the Offline Store during real-time fraud inference. S3 Athena queries take seconds! Query the Online Store for live predictions.

tasks.title: Skill 1.2.7: Document Preparation for RAG (Chunking & Metadata Extraction)
tasks.topic: Domain 1: Data Preparation for ML & AI
tasks.subtopic: Task 1.2: Perform data transformation, feature engineering, and pre-processing
tasks.description: RAG (Retrieval Augmented Generation) answers questions using private company docs. Before storing documents in a vector DB, you must slice them into chunks. Fixed-size chunking splits by word count (with overlap so sentences aren't cut in half). Hierarchical / semantic chunking splits by headers or paragraphs. Metadata (author, section, date) is attached for filtered search.
tasks.notes: Exam Tip: Always include chunk overlap (typically 10-20%) to preserve conversational and semantic context. Gotcha: Chunking without overlap. Without overlap, questions matching ideas split across chunk boundaries will fail retrieval!

tasks.description: Bias happens when a dataset unfairly favors or discriminates against a specific group (e.g. approving loans for one demographic at twice the rate). SageMaker Clarify analyzes pre-training data bias (like Class Imbalance [CI], Difference in Proportions of Labels [DPL]) and post-training model prediction bias (Disparate Impact [DI]).
tasks.notes: Exam Tip: Use SageMaker Clarify for both pre-training and post-training bias analysis and model explainability (SHAP). Gotcha: Assuming Clarify automatically modifies data to fix bias. Clarify DETECTS and METRICIZES bias; you must apply resampling or reweighting!

tasks.subtopic: Security, Identity, and Compliance
tasks.description: AWS Key Management Service (KMS) protects all your ML data at rest. You create Customer Managed Keys (CMKs) that give you full control over key rotation and IAM access policies.
tasks.notes: Role: Cryptographic service for managing encryption keys (CMKs) across S3 data, EBS volumes, ECR images, and SageMaker models. Exam Tip: SageMaker execution roles need explicit `kms:Decrypt` and `kms:GenerateDataKey` permissions for CMK-encrypted buckets. Gotcha: Forgetting to grant `kms:Decrypt` permission to the SageMaker execution role. If the S3 bucket is encrypted with a KMS CMK, the role will fail with Access Denied!

tasks.title: Amazon S3

tasks.description: Amazon S3 is the bedrock of all AWS ML architectures. It stores raw training data, holds final model tarballs, saves training checkpoints for Spot instances, and hosts your offline feature store.
